fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (docs/evidence/flags-evaluation-2-2026-11-08, friction 1): crates/batter/examples/rollout.rs starts its supervisor directly and migrates with a hand-built pool, while the facade and control_plane rustdoc point to Startup::protected and command::Command; no example combines the HTTP gate, the job gate and a pin. Make the example the canonical consumer contract for the control plane: protected startup, a finite migrate command, the route-group gate, a gated job and a pinned decision resolved in the handler.
fields.title: Show the protected startup path and every flags surface in one facade example

fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (friction 2): JobFlags has no test constructor and the worker-free handler drive needs runledger-test-support, whose Docker crates are not resolvable offline, so a consumer cannot test its gated handler itself. Provide a fixture path (for example TestFlags producing JobFlags) that reaches a GatedHandler without a database or Docker, without weakening the protected path.
fields.title: Give JobFlags a test constructor and drive a gated job handler offline

fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (friction 3): job_phases(...)?.into_operation(work, finalize) takes owned callbacks, which a FlagAwareHandler that borrows JobFlags and reads its pin from the row first cannot use, so the consumer fell back to the manual sequencing batter-runledger labels not the protected path. Assess a protected composition of flag-aware handlers with invocation phases (ADR-010).
fields.title: Let a flag-aware job handler use the protected job_phases path

fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (friction 4): before the first publication GatedHandler always fails the attempt with its awaiting recheck, whatever DirectWhenTripped says (amendment A3 item 4), so a long first-boot outage of the flags store can dead-letter jobs. Owner decision: keep attempt consumption (disclosed in ADR-016), or allow an explicit continue-without-attempt policy for the awaiting window.
fields.title: Decide whether a gated job may continue rather than consume attempts before the first flags publication

fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (friction 5-7): the batter-flags command's JSON payloads (show state encoding, history after rows, fleet --version fields, proposed_version on uncertain outcomes) are undocumented; 're-run with --if-revision' does not say to use the original revision, whose safety rests on the store answering an already-satisfied write unchanged before its revision check (stated only in batter-flags-postgres's README); and failed reads report 'nothing written' and show a refused connection as a timeout.
fields.title: Document the operator command's JSON, its retry revision and read-failure wording

fields.description: Flags evaluation 2 (friction 8): flags-postgres selects no TLS provider, so a consumer cannot use sslmode=verify-full through the facade alone; no helper yields today's CivilDate; sharing SQLx's migration ledger with the application's own migrator is undocumented; narrowing settings before declared::resolve silently resets flags to their defaults (stated only in rustdoc); SharedCommandReport has no Display.
fields.title: Close the smaller flags consumer gaps from evaluation 2
